title.narrative: Multi-purpose cash Assistance for PwDs in Severe need (MAPS)

description.narrative: ltpgtThe MAPS project will provide approximately 920 households (5,520 individuals including 1,546 women, 1,546 men, 1,214 girls, and 1,214 boys) with multipurpose cash assistance (MPCA) in Deir ez-Zour to cover basic lifesaving and life-sustaining needs of food items, WASH and hygiene products, health and other essential non-food items (NFIs). ADRA will provide monthly assistance ($100 or equivalent in SYP) to the targeted families for five months through local financial service providers (FSPs) or banks, aiming to reduce their reliance on negative coping mechanisms. A total of 1,176 Persons with Disabilities (PwD) are expected to benefit within the targeted households. ltbrgtThis project will target an extremely vulnerable group, PWDs, thereby contributing to their protection by helping them obtain essential goods and reducing their reliance on negative coping mechanisms. This is especially critical as Deir ez-Zour’s is one of the areas with the highest need areas in the country, and limited humanitarian actors. In providing this aid, the MAPS project will therefore contribute to strategic priority one of the allocation strategy – to support and strengthen the delivery of critical basic services to ensure the most vulnerable populations in underserved locations affected by conflict, displacement, and natural shocks, receive integrated life-saving and life-sustaining humanitarian aid.ltbrgtThe project design was based on a general needs assessment, market assessment and household level assessment from potential beneficiaries which verified the urgent need for assistance, the suitability of the planned intervention (MPCA) and the appropriateness (functioning market and availability of FSPs).ltbrgtADRA is an active member of the Cash Working Group with extensive experience implementing MPCA projects in the region. ADRA maintains a field office in Deir ez-Zour with several full-time staff under the area manager. ADRA likewise has full access to all populated government-controlled areas where this project targets, and has existing agreements with MoSAL that simplify and expedite the approval process for activities. This project will be implemented in tandem with existing activities in Deir ez-Zour, including education in emergencies (EiE) programming, as well as the provision of assistive devices for highly vulnerable persons with disabilities (PWDs). ADRA has previously implemented several MPCA assistance project in 2020/2021 in Damascus and Rural Damascus, in 2021/2022 Homs and Hama and in 2023/2024 in Latakia. ltbrgtlt/pgt
